headline: ACC probe into Asif Mahmud over alleged corruption
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has launched an investigation into irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports, naming former interim adviser Asif Mahmud.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has launched an investigation into alleged corruption and irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports.
Former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan is among four officials under probe, making him the first former interim adviser to face such an inquiry.
The allegations include corruption in recruitment, promotions, appointments, and procurement through a syndicate, according to ACC Deputy Director Akhtarul Islam.
The complaint alleges that Tk 76 lakh was taken for transferring 38 upazila youth development officers and Tk 1.5 crore for promoting 150 assistant officers.
It is further alleged that another Tk 2 crore for securing preferred postings after promotion was collected.
Asif Mahmud, spokesperson of the National Citizen Party, has denied all allegations, calling them politically motivated.
He has given the ACC a 24-hour ultimatum to apologize for defaming him, and warned he would serve a legal notice if they fail to do so.
Despite the dispute, Asif Mahmud stated he is ready to cooperate with any lawful inquiry and provide all relevant documents.
caption:
A former interim government adviser is under investigation for corruption. Asif Mahmud denies the claims and threatens legal action.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has launched an investigation into alleged corruption and irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports.

Former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan is among four officials under probe, making him the first former interim adviser to face such an inquiry.

The allegations include corruption in recruitment, promotions, appointments, and procurement through a syndicate, according to ACC Deputy Director Akhtarul Islam.

The complaint alleges that Tk 76 lakh was taken for transferring 38 upazila youth development officers and Tk 1.5 crore for promoting 150 assistant officers.

It is further alleged that another Tk 2 crore for securing preferred postings after promotion was collected.

Asif Mahmud, spokesperson of the National Citizen Party, has denied all allegations, calling them politically motivated.

He has given the ACC a 24-hour ultimatum to apologize for defaming him, and warned he would serve a legal notice if they fail to do so.

Despite the dispute, Asif Mahmud stated he is ready to cooperate with any lawful inquiry and provide all relevant documents.

headline_marked: [[Homeopathic practitioner hacked to death]] in Natore
headline: Homeopathic practitioner hacked to death in Natore
summary: Md Anwarul Islam, 60, was killed in his chamber at Chandpur Market on Wednesday night; police say the motive remains unclear.
details: A 60-year-old homeopathic practitioner, Md Anwarul Islam, was hacked to death in his chamber at Chandpur Market in Natore Sadar upazila on Wednesday night.
The attack occurred around 7:30 pm while the victim was working in his chamber, according to Md Monsur Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Natore Sadar Police Station.
Police recovered the body and sent it to Natore Sadar Hospital for an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death.
Md Anwarul Islam, originally from Puthia upazila in Rajshahi, had been practicing homeopathy in the Chandpur Bazar area for over three decades.
Locals reported that the victim typically arrived at his shop in the afternoon and remained open until 9:00 pm.
According to residents, they were unaware of any enmity or specific motive that would lead to the attack.
Police are currently investigating the incident and working to identify the culprits, as no witnesses have yet come forward.
